sections.history: Tirumanancheri lies in Chola Nadu on the north bank of the Kaveri, a few kilometres from Kuthalam on the road between Kumbakonam and Mayiladuthurai. The name is read as the settlement of the wedding, and the Tevaram hymns of Appar and Sambandar praise the Lord here, which makes the temple a Paadal Petra Sthalam. Tradition holds that the first shrine was raised in brick in the age of the saints, in the seventh century, and that it was rebuilt in stone in the Chola period, around the time of Parantaka I. Inscriptions record gifts under Parantaka I and Rajaraja I, among them the endowment of the Chola queen Sembiyan Mahadevi, and later Pandya, Hoysala and Nayak patrons also served the temple.
sections.architecture: The temple is a Dravidian stone structure facing east, entered through a gopuram into the courtyard where the sanctum of Udhvaganathar, also called Kalyanasundareswarar, the Lord as the beautiful bridegroom, stands beside the separate shrine of the goddess Kokilambal. She is honoured here in the grace of a bride, and the whole temple is arranged around the idea of the wedding. The sacred water is the Saptasagara tirtham, said to hold the seven seas that came to witness the marriage. The sacred trees of the place are the dhatura, the vanni and the konrai. Detailed measurements of the enclosure and gopuram are not given in the sources consulted.
sections.legends: The legend of Tirumanancheri is the wedding of Shiva and Parvati. Tradition says that the goddess, at Kailasa, asked to be wed to the Lord once more upon the earth, and he gave his word without naming the time or the place. After a moment of lapse she was sent down to the earth in the form of a cow, and only after her penance and prayer was she restored. At Tirumanancheri the Lord appeared as Kalyanasundarar, the beautiful bridegroom, and took the goddess as Kokilambal in marriage, while the gods and sages gathered and the seven seas arrived to witness the union. For this reason the village is called the place of the wedding, and the Lord is Udhvaganathar, from udhvaha, marriage.
sections.festivals: The great festival is the Chithirai Thirukalyanam, the wedding of the Lord and goddess, held over three days in April or May and centred on the Poosam star. On the eve of the wedding the Lord is taken in procession as the bridegroom to the neighbouring village of Edirkolpadi, where the priest receives him as the father of the bride with the honours of the full pot, and only then does he return to wed the goddess. Aadi Pooram, Tiruvadhirai and Tirukarthigai are also observed, with Maha Shivaratri and the monthly Pradosham. Confirm dates locally, as they follow the Tamil calendar.
sections.experience: Tirumanancheri is a temple of hope, and it is busy with families and young people who have come to pray for a good marriage. The customary offering is a garland placed upon the Lord, with archana, after which the garland is taken home and kept with faith; once the marriage has taken place, devotees return with the old garland to give thanks. The wedding is re-enacted in the temple every day, and the atmosphere is that of a family occasion more than of a solemn visit. Come early, move slowly through the shrines of the Lord and Kokilambal, and sit awhile by the tirtham in the quiet that follows the crowd.

visit.timings: Typically open in the morning and again from late afternoon into the evening, with a midday break; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days and on auspicious wedding dates when the temple is crowded.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected: dhotis or trousers for men, sarees, salwar kameez, or long skirts for women, with shoulders and knees covered. Footwear is left at the entrance stands.
visit.photography: Photography is generally permitted in the outer corridors and courtyards but prohibited inside the inner sanctum, in keeping with Tamil Nadu temple rules. Ask temple staff before photographing rituals, priests or devotees.
visit.gettingThere: Tirumanancheri is about 5 km from Kuthalam on the Kumbakonam–Mayiladuthurai road, roughly 25 to 30 km from Kumbakonam. Mayiladuthurai, a larger railway junction, is the nearest main station, and Kumbakonam is the other convenient base. Buses and taxis serve the village from both towns. The nearest major airport is Tiruchirappalli, a few hours away by road.
